newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures down, but not out following strong M3.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures down, but not out following strong M3.

text.p: German Bund futures survived suprisingly strong August money supply growth on Thursday to trade only marginally lower in late trade.

Traders said Bunds remained buoyant because the market still believes money supply remains on an easing trend despite 8.7 percent growth in August and other indicators such as the Ifo survey raised little worry about inflation.
The DTB December Bund future was down eight basis points late in the day to 97.99, well off a low of 97.87 reached immediately following the M3 release.
Indeed, Bunds clawed back almost all the M3-related loss after the Ifo research institute's business climate index climbed to 94.4 from a revised 94.0 in July.

Although the Ifo figure was within expectations, market talk just before the release had been for a much stronger figure and Bunds climbed when the market saw the fears had been unfounded. "M3 has maybe lost some of its importance to other indicators such as the Ifo report," said Peter Kerger, portfolio manager at Credit Suisse.
He and others said they see support for the contract at 97.90.

Analysts said underlying data in the M3 figure showed that money growth should continue to slow. "The (limited) size of the market's dip after M3 came out shows the market was not that worried," said Timo Klein, analyst at MMS International.

Traders said they expected to see renewed interest in the long-end of the yield curve. The yield curve, which is steep by historical standards, could flatten as investors become more comfortable with the prospect of European monetary union, one trader said.
The spread between Bunds and their U.S. counterparts widened to minus 79 basis points from minus 76 basis points.
